name: Monili Jewellers
tagline: 1,228 products. Two major phases. A luxury platform migrated, rebuilt, and redesigned in production code.
shortDescription: Took a luxury jewellery platform off a restrictive third-party system, rebuilt every interactive frontend from scratch on a custom Laravel/Vue stack, then redesigned the entire interface in production code — delivering a faster, more premium experience across 1,228 products.
challenge: Monili Jewellers was locked into a third-party e-commerce platform that couldn't support the frontend complexity or performance standards a luxury catalogue of 1,228 products demanded. Core Web Vitals were poor, mobile responsiveness was unreliable, and the visual direction no longer matched the quality of the jewellery.
approach: Delivered in two phases. Phase 1 migrated the platform to a custom Laravel/Vue decoupled architecture, rebuilding every stateful frontend system from scratch — mega navigation, live search, cart, checkout, and customer accounts. Phase 2 redesigned the entire frontend directly in production code, introducing refined spacing, stronger typography, and a more premium visual direction without disrupting the backend.
outcome: +25% sessions after frontend restructuring. +21% user growth. ~52% sustained engagement rate. Repair inquiry interactions increased after the dedicated flow launched.
highlights: Migrated from third-party platform to custom Laravel/Vue decoupled architecture
Built full stateful frontend: mega nav, live search, cart, checkout, customer accounts
Phase 2 in-code redesign introduced refined spacing, typography, and visual alignment
Reduced layout instability to near-zero CLS across product-heavy pages
Designed 481 social media assets across Instagram, LinkedIn, and Facebook
performance: Reduced CLS to near-zero across product pages. Configured lazy loading and optimised image delivery to improve LCP. Removed render-blocking assets across the catalogue.
seo: Clean, semantic frontend architecture across 1,228 products supporting improved search indexability.

name: Scandinavian Physiotherapy Center
tagline: 11.1s to 0.6s. A healthcare website rebuilt from the infrastructure up.
shortDescription: Rebuilt a physiotherapy clinic's website from scratch — fixing years of technical debt, restructuring content around how patients actually search, and turning organic search into the clinic's primary acquisition channel.
role: Web Design · Frontend Development · Email Marketing
challenge: By 2025, the clinic's website was running on borrowed time. Legacy code caused layout shifts, broken forms dropped patient submissions, fragmented treatment pages offered nothing for search engines, and there was no clear path from landing on the site to booking an appointment.
approach: Started with the foundation: rebuilt from scratch on a clean WordPress architecture with SEO-optimised URL structures. Transformed thin treatment pages into structured editorial content. Fixed heading hierarchy, blog templates, and broken links. Reduced LCP from 11.1s to 0.6s. Designed and coded responsive HTML email newsletters as a patient retention channel.
outcome: 15K organic sessions/month. +67.9% key conversion events. 3.1K active users/month. LCP reduced from 11.1s to 0.6s. Performance 80, SEO 92, Accessibility 94.
highlights: Rebuilt site from scratch with clean URL architecture based on SEO audit
Transformed fragmented treatment pages into structured editorial content
Reduced LCP from 11.1s to 0.6s — CLS stabilised to 0
Built 8 homepage drafts in Figma to refine the final direction
Designed and coded responsive HTML email newsletters for patient retention
Standardised booking entry points across all key pages
accessibility: Accessibility score of 94 achieved. Content restructured with proper heading hierarchy and semantic markup throughout.
performance: LCP reduced from 11.1s to 0.6s. CLS dropped to 0. Performance score improved from <50 to 80. Legacy images converted to modern formats with lazy loading.
seo: Restructured routing into clean semantic URLs. Fixed blog templates, heading hierarchy, and broken links. SEO score reached 92.

name: Rocky Real Estate
tagline: 89% organic traffic. A property platform rebuilt around how Dubai buyers actually search.
shortDescription: Rebuilt a high-traffic Dubai property platform from scratch — stripping years of plugin bloat, implementing technical SEO infrastructure, building a modular campaign system, and making organic search the dominant acquisition channel across four years of continuous management.
challenge: Rocky Real Estate had 44 years of market presence trapped behind a website carrying years of technical debt — bloated plugins, fragmented page architecture, no structured enquiry path, and no scalable way to launch campaigns for new property developments.
approach: Rebuilt the platform from scratch on a custom WordPress theme. Connected the CRM to frontend listing templates alongside a backend developer. Implemented clean URL structures, schema markup, XML sitemaps, and GA4 funnel tracking. Built a modular campaign page system for property launches. Managed and optimised the platform continuously for four years.
outcome: 48K total users. 43K organic users — 89% of all inbound traffic. 36 high-intent enquiries tracked. Platform managed and optimised over 4 continuous years.
highlights: Rebuilt platform from scratch on a clean custom WordPress theme
Implemented technical SEO: clean URLs, schema markup, XML sitemap, GA4 funnel tracking
Connected CRM to frontend listing templates with backend developer
Built reusable campaign landing page system for property launches
43K organic users — 89% of all platform traffic
Managed and optimised platform continuously for 4 years
performance: Removed legacy plugin bloat for a lightweight, maintainable codebase. GA4 tracking across scroll depth and listing engagement.
seo: Clean semantic URL structures, schema markup, XML sitemap, and structured heading hierarchy. Organic search became the dominant acquisition channel.

name: P&O Marinas
tagline: A DP World marina that buried its core service. Rebuilt around berth rental with a custom interactive map.
shortDescription: Rebuilt the digital presence for a DP World marina company across two phases — implementing a new corporate brand system, restructuring the platform around berth rental as the core commercial service, and delivering a custom interactive SVG berth map.
challenge: P&O Marinas had a website that presented the brand but buried the business. Berth rental — the marina's primary commercial offering — had no dedicated page, no booking journey, and no digital tool for exploring availability. The brand experience was fragmented across inconsistent layouts.
approach: Phase 1 revamped the existing site and managed social media design. Phase 2 implemented a new corporate brand identity from scratch, rebuilt every page, restructured the platform around berth rental as the core service, and delivered a custom interactive SVG berth map — defining data fields, coordinating backend implementation, and QA'ing against the actual marina layout.
outcome: 8K total users with organic as dominant acquisition. 4 new core pages launched. 1 custom interactive berth map live. 481 social media assets designed across two years.
highlights: Identified berth rental as the platform's core commercial service gap
Implemented complete brand identity system across all pages
Built, QA'd, and signed off custom interactive SVG berth map with availability states
Launched 4 new core pages: Berth, Berth Process, Cruise Terminal, Mina Rashid Lifestyle
Designed 481 social media assets across Instagram, LinkedIn, and Facebook

name: Vijit Pillai Art
tagline: 35+ screens, zero starting point. A gallery-grade art platform designed and built from scratch.
shortDescription: Designed a complete art-commerce platform for an internationally recognised artist — 35+ screens spanning storefront and custom admin — then built the full customer-facing frontend in React/TSX.
challenge: An internationally recognised contemporary artist with 750+ artworks collected across five countries had no dedicated digital channel. Sales and enquiries were handled through fragmented informal channels with no inventory system, no checkout, and no way to scale.
approach: Designed the platform to feel like a physical gallery — large imagery, generous spacing, minimalist direction. Created 35+ high-fidelity screens covering the complete customer journey and a full admin panel. Built the storefront frontend in React/TSX, worked closely with the backend developer throughout, and QA'd the entire platform against designs before launch.
outcome: Complete art-commerce platform from zero: 35+ screens, full customer purchase journey, and artist admin covering inventory, orders, customers, newsletter, and site settings.

name: Nuraya Properties
tagline: A logo and nothing else. Brand, bilingual website, analytics, and infrastructure — all built in one engagement.
shortDescription: Established the complete digital foundation for a new Dubai real estate brand — developing a visual identity from a single logo, building a bilingual English/French WordPress platform, configuring analytics from day one, and deploying the full production infrastructure.
challenge: Nuraya Properties entered the Dubai market with a logo and nothing else — no website, no brand guidelines, no hosting, no analytics, no business email. The English/French bilingual requirement meant the foundation had to support two audiences from launch.
approach: Built the visual identity system using the logo as the only reference point. Developed a custom WordPress theme — no page builders, no templates. Integrated bilingual content with natural language switching. Configured GA4 at launch to capture early traction. Deployed everything to production: hosting, domain, DNS, forms, and email.
outcome: +30% active users. +54% events tracked. +61% page views. +117% user engagement in first tracked month. 5+ countries reached. France in top 5 from month one. +50% organic sessions, zero paid.
highlights: Developed complete visual system from a single logo with no existing brand guidelines
Built custom WordPress theme — no page builders or templates
Implemented bilingual (English/French) architecture in a single WordPress installation
Configured GA4 from day one with full event and channel attribution
Deployed to production: hosting, domain, DNS, forms, and email systems
France reached top 5 visitor countries within the first tracked month

name: Althea Diamonds
tagline: A lab-grown diamond brand that didn't exist yet. Logo to live Shopify store.
shortDescription: Created the complete brand identity and e-commerce experience for a new Dubai lab-grown diamond jewellery company — designing the visual system from scratch, building the Shopify storefront through Liquid customisation, and supporting product photography production.
challenge: Althea Diamonds entered the Dubai jewellery market with nothing — no logo, no visual identity, no e-commerce platform, no product imagery. Lab-grown diamonds still require trust-building from first visit, making brand credibility non-negotiable.
approach: Designed the logo from scratch and built a complete visual identity system — typography, colour palette, spacing, and hierarchy. Built and customised the Shopify storefront via Liquid template edits. Structured product pages, collections, cart, and checkout around the brand system. Participated in product photography production to ensure visual consistency at launch.
outcome: Complete brand and Shopify platform launched from scratch — logo, visual identity, storefront, product photography, and consistent brand language across every customer touchpoint.
highlights: Designed brand identity from scratch — logo, typography, colour palette, visual system
Built Shopify storefront via Liquid template customisation — not just CSS
Product pages, collections, cart, and checkout aligned to the brand system
Participated in product photography production for visual consistency
Applied consistent brand language across all customer touchpoints from launch
accessibility: Interactive elements including ring-size selection built with keyboard accessibility and clear labels.

name: Tip2Gether
tagline: No wireframes, no specs, no prior product. A tipping platform designed from a blank brief.
shortDescription: Designed and built a football tipping platform from a blank brief — defining how predictions, scoring, live match updates, and leaderboard systems work, then building the frontend across a six-month collaboration with a backend developer.
challenge: Nothing existed — no wireframes, no user flows, no predefined rules for how any of it should work. The platform needed to handle three distinct match states, a competitive points system, and real-time leaderboard movement while remaining intuitive for casual users.
approach: Defined the complete product experience from scratch. Designed a three-state match system — upcoming, live, completed — as the core structural decision. Built reusable frontend components that adapted to each state, integrated with the Laravel backend for live scoring, and collaborated with the backend developer across the full six-month build.
outcome: Complete football tipping platform launched and active for a full Bundesliga 2 season — tipping interface, live score display, automated points system, leaderboard, and match history all shipped.
highlights: Designed the full product from a blank brief — no prior wireframes or specifications
Defined three-state match system (upcoming, live, completed) as the core product architecture
Built reusable frontend components adapting dynamically to each match state
Implemented tipping flow, live score display, leaderboard, and match history
Six-month collaboration with backend developer across full implementation and QA

tagline: Multiple directions, multiple review rounds, one approved system — WCAG AA from the start.
shortDescription: Designed a corporate website through structured stakeholder review — developing and presenting multiple homepage concepts, refining typography and layout across iterative feedback rounds, and documenting the approved direction for full-site rollout.
challenge: The brief wasn't a single direction to execute — it was an open question. Multiple homepage concepts had to be developed and defended, balancing competing priorities around typography, image prominence, and layout hierarchy, all while maintaining WCAG AA compliance across every direction.
approach: Developed and presented multiple homepage design concepts with distinct typography directions. Tested and refined image weights, spacing, and visual hierarchy in response to each round of stakeholder feedback. Coordinated the design selection process and prepared the approved direction for consistent rollout across the remaining website pages.
outcome: A cohesive corporate visual identity with a clear information hierarchy, approved through structured stakeholder review, and documented for consistent implementation across the full site.
highlights: Multiple homepage design concepts developed and presented
Typography and layout refined across iterative review rounds
Image prominence, spacing, and hierarchy adjusted per feedback
Approved direction prepared and documented for full-site rollout
accessibility: Typographic contrast ratios and heading hierarchy evaluated during the design phase to meet WCAG AA requirements.

name: Transgulf
tagline: The content search engines couldn't read. Vue components converted to crawlable HTML.
shortDescription: Fixed the invisible problems on a corporate transport website — converting business-critical content trapped inside Vue components into crawlable HTML, correcting on-page SEO signals, and resolving responsive layout issues across tablet breakpoints.
challenge: The site looked complete, but its most valuable content — office addresses, contact information, company details — was embedded inside Vue components that rendered for visitors but were invisible to search engines. Tablet layouts were structurally broken, and a third-party script was fighting the CSS.
approach: Worked within the existing Vue architecture to surface key content as crawlable semantic HTML without requiring a re-platform. Updated homepage headings, title tags, and meta descriptions. Fixed responsive header, footer, and banner behaviour across tablet breakpoints. Made office addresses interactive with Google Maps links. Removed the third-party script causing layout interference.
outcome: Business-critical content made crawlable. On-page SEO signals corrected. Consistent layout behaviour restored across tablet and mobile. Third-party script removed, reducing JavaScript load.
highlights: Converted essential content to crawlable semantic HTML
Updated title tags and meta descriptions for key pages
Fixed responsive header, footer, and banner on tablet
Office addresses made interactive with Google Maps links
Removed third-party script causing layout interference
accessibility: Ensured address and contact information was accessible as semantic text rather than embedded within image or script-rendered components.
performance: Removed a third-party responsive preview script, reducing unnecessary JavaScript load.
seo: Updated site structure, title tags, and meta descriptions. Converted non-crawlable content to semantic HTML, improving indexability of key pages.
